correctness.rationale: Exact first integral and proper potential give every global oval. Canonical time-preserving transformation yields G(q)/q strictly increasing, so the original-time period decreases strictly. Exact u=A^2-x^2 quadrature gives a representation uniformly parametrized by r=gamma A^2/(1+gamma A^2) in (0,1). Weighted Taylor bounds with exponentially small tails yield a uniform O_beta(A^-4) relative remainder; all required beta integrals are evaluated explicitly. A standalone script from the actual package checks symbolic steps and 18 numerical quadratures but cannot prove an infinite asymptotic. Quantifiers: fixed beta>0, any gamma>0 (including gamma(A) when evaluating uniform formula), amplitude A->infinity. No beta-down-to-zero uniformity claimed.

originality.rationale: The assessed contribution is strictly for gamma>0: an all-amplitude decreasing-period theorem and an explicit two-term original-time high-amplitude expansion with remainder uniform in gamma>0, including gamma*A^2=O(1). The axis gamma=0 is implied by existing published mathematical results and excluded from novelty. The defining full-text source establishes global-center existence, and the closest public full result texts cover other parameter families; none of the inspected statements implies the gamma-dependent coefficient (2 log 2 - 1) r /(2 beta). Residual risks remain for unindexed or broader period-function criteria.
residual_risks: Relevant broad period-function literature can imply qualitative strict monotonicity, and an unexamined general theorem may supply the present uniform second-order coefficient.
The 2013 Lienard-period article was inspected only at abstract level, not declared not covering on full-document grounds.
Unindexed equivalent work or unpublished mathematical results may alter publication priority.
The result is new only for strictly positive cubic-restoring coefficient gamma, not for gamma=0, whose two-term period law is known.

value.rationale: The turning-point period is an intrinsic invariant of each cubic-center oval and determines physical recurrence frequency. The two different principal scalings A^-1 and A^-2 require resolving the transition gamma A^2=O(1), not simply evaluating a fixed-parameter limit. The uniform two-term formula finds the exact crossover in the first relative correction, absent from the known beta-only axis; strict decrease proves uniqueness at every prescribed nontrivial period. The precise parameter crossover and correction are motivated by competing cubic restoration and velocity-dependent feedback, not an arbitrary small slice or known table recomputation.
